glosses: Plaisanter, raconter des galéjades.

examples.text: Quatre-vingt-deux paires dans une seule maison?! Tu galèjes!?

Allons ! Maintenant suffit, assez galéjé,
Vous allez d’une toute autre façon chanter.

Eh bien, j’ai le plaisir, preuve à l’appui, de m’inscrire en faux contre cette maligne assertion. Ceux qui l’affirment, l’assènent à tout bout de champ, le proclament à l’envi ont la langue plus fourchue que vipère aspic, ils galèjent mieux que Marseillais à la pétanque, ils ne sont que vils baratineurs, ils mythonent, pipeautent, racontent des craques ou accrochent des paletots.

glosses: An act performed for amusement; a joke.

examples.text: I made that comment in jest; it wasn't serious.
Alas poore Yorick, I knew him Horatio, a fellow of infinite Ieſt; […]

glosses: Someone or something that is ridiculed; the target of a joke.

examples.text: Your majesty, stop him before he makes you the jest of the court.
Why then make ſport at me, then let me be your ieſt, / I deſerue it[…]

glosses: A deed; an action; a gest.

examples.text: the jests or actions of princes

glosses: A mask; a pageant; an interlude.

examples.text: He promised us, in honour of our guest, / To grace our banquet with some pompous jest.

glosses: To tell a joke; to talk in a playful manner; to make fun of something or someone.

examples.text: Surely you jest!

glosses: Pronunciation spelling of just.

examples.text: So I jest called out to know what was up, and found it was Miss Vanholte's cowboys, who had been forced into the store by them rascally ruffins.
"Jest like the Injian puzzle-boxes, ain't they?" said Dan, as the one boat dropped into the other.

glosses: An amusing story.

examples.text: Or witty joke our airy senses moves / To pleasant laughter.

glosses: Something said or done for amusement, not in seriousness.

examples.text: It was a joke!

glosses: The root cause or main issue, especially an unexpected one
A laughably worthless thing or person; a sham.

examples.text: Your effort at cleaning your room is a joke.
The president was a joke.
The other wheel on the tender of the L.N.W.R. engines operated the tender brake, and this was always rather a joke. Sometimes it operated with good results and on other occasions it did not.

glosses: Something that is far easier or far less challenging than expected.

examples.text: The final exam was a joke.

glosses: To do or say something for amusement rather than seriously.

examples.text: I didn’t mean what I said — I was only joking.

glosses: To dupe in a friendly manner for amusement; to mess with, play with.

examples.text: Relax, man, I'm just joking with you.

glosses: To make merry with; to make jokes upon; to rally.

examples.text: to joke a comrade

He made more than one visit to Oxbridge, where the young fellows were amused by entertaining the old gentleman, and gave parties and breakfasts and fêtes, partly to joke him and partly to do him honour.

glosses: To tease, ridicule or make jokes about, generally in a pejorative manner.

examples.text: Please stop making fun of your sister and just help her!

glosses: Đùa vui một cách tinh nghịch.
